provenance.sourceQuality: Fresh Reuters, AP and WSJ reports dated November 25; prior cash, VXN, WTI and NQ observations explicitly carried forward. Open Watch verified unchanged. No synchronized live cross-asset panel.
provenance.marketVsCatalyst: Asian losses observed; tariff outcome and PCE response pending.

editorial.marketOverview: Asian technology markets remain under pressure following Tuesday's US semiconductor losses. Reuters reports negative S&P futures and lower Brent; the prior Nasdaq futures indication remains historical. Cash trading has not begun.
editorial.whatChanged: Fresh WSJ reporting shows lower paired Treasury yields, while Reuters and AP corroborate the already recorded Asian technology selloff. The tariff risk is not new relative to the previous assessment. Open Watch remains at 178 events with no new curated catalyst.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The reported 10Y and 2Y yields imply a positive 23.8 bp curve. Lower yields ease valuation pressure but may also reflect defensive demand; semiconductor leadership remains weak. No synchronized QQQ, SOX or VXN quote establishes a reversal.
editorial.threeDayPath: Wednesday has a bearish tilt ahead of PCE and GDP. Friday's shortened session raises liquidity risk; Monday is the next normal session to test whether chip leadership returns.
editorial.bullCase: Benign inflation and lower yields could trigger a rebound if semiconductor participation broadens and volatility eases. Dell demand provides fundamental support but is not sufficient alone.
editorial.bearCase: Further tariff escalation or sticky inflation could reinforce chip liquidation and extend QQQ weakness into Friday and Monday. Asian declines are observed, not a guarantee of US losses.
editorial.watchNext: Monitor PCE and GDP at 08:30 ET, actual tariff announcements, SOX relative to QQQ, breadth and VXN/VIX. Refresh paired yields and oil before drawing cross-asset conclusions.
